title: RBI Survey of Professional Forecasters: Real GDP Growth
description: Median forecast of annual real GDP growth (per cent, constant prices) by professional forecasters in the Reserve Bank's Survey of Professional Forecasters. Each point is the median forecast of the panel in one survey round, stamped on the first day of the month in which the survey was conducted (the press release follows 4-6 weeks later). The 'current fiscal year' series is the forecast for the April-March year that contains the survey month (e.g. a September 2026 round gives 2026-27); 'next fiscal year' is the following year. So the series is the evolution of expectations, not a time series of outcomes: the forecast target changes each April. Useful as the consensus benchmark against which to judge nowcasts and official estimates.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Survey of Professional Forecasters press releases)

qna.question: What is the Survey of Professional Forecasters?
qna.answer: A Reserve Bank survey of about 30-50 economists from banks, research houses and rating agencies, who forecast growth, inflation, external and financial variables for the current and following fiscal years and the next few quarters. The Reserve Bank has run it since September 2007.^The press release reports the median forecast (with mean, range and quartiles in annexes). This series takes the median from the annual-forecast annexes.

qna.question: How do I read the points?
qna.answer: Each point is one survey round: the date is the survey month and the value is the median forecast of growth for the fiscal year named in the series (current or next). Moves between rounds show how forecasters are revising in response to data.^Watch the gap between current- and next-year forecasts, and the size of revisions after GDP releases or policy shocks.

qna.question: What are the caveats?
qna.answer: The fiscal year is the April-March year, and GDP is real GDP at constant prices. The base year and definition of GDP change when the national accounts are rebased, so forecasts across a rebasing are not strictly comparable.^The panel membership varies by round and views are the forecasters' own, not the Reserve Bank's.
